title: version set destroys an unrecognised sidecar and the gate then certifies it clean
body:
# 0002: version set destroys an unrecognised sidecar and the gate then certifies it clean

## Tags

version, sidecars, false-green, WP-10, blocker

## Summary

`write_version_into` (`lib/cmd/version`) carries recipes for `Cargo.toml`, `mix.exs`, `package.json` and `*.plist`, and a default branch that writes the bare version string over the whole file. Conflab declares two `Cargo.lock` sidecars, which hit that default: the first `version` command WP-10 runs against Conflab overwrites both lockfiles with a five-byte version string, and every gate reports success. Found during WP-10 preparation, by running the command rather than reading it.

**The default itself is deliberate, documented and tested, and this issue does not ask for it to be removed.** `docs/configuration.md:41` states it plainly -- devbin knows five recipes "and treats anything else as a bare version string" -- and `tests/unit/version.bats:144` declares a `plain.txt` sidecar seeded with a bare version and asserts the write lands. A project with a second plain version file is a real case and that is the case the default serves.

What is wrong is narrower and worse: devbin cannot tell a bare version file from a structured file it has no recipe for, it resolves that ambiguity by destroying the second kind, and its own gate then certifies the result as correct.

## Reproduction

A scratch install (devbin 0.1.0), a `Cargo.lock` declared in `project.version_sidecars`:

```
$ cat native/cli/Cargo.lock          # 10 lines
# This file is automatically @generated by Cargo.
version = 3

[[package]]
name = "lockprobe"
version = "0.6.0"
...

$ bin/devbin version set 0.7.0
0.7.0
$ echo $?
0

$ cat native/cli/Cargo.lock          # 1 line
0.7.0
```

The read side fails in the mirror image. `read_version` has the same default branch, so `tr -d '[:space:]'` mashes the whole lockfile into one token and reports it as the version:

```
$ bin/devbin version check
  native/cli/Cargo.lock   #Thisfileisautomatically@generatedbyCargo.version=3[[package]]name="lockprobe"version="0.6.0" (expected 0.6.0)
lockprobe: version sidecars have drifted (heal with: lockprobe version sync)
```

The two halves compose into the sharpest form of the defect. Every step behaves as designed:

```
1. version check   ->  rc=1  "sidecars have drifted (heal with: ... version sync)"
2. version sync    ->  rc=0  destroys the lockfile
3. version check   ->  rc=0  "version: 0.6.0, every sidecar agrees"
```

The command tells the user to run the thing that destroys their file, then certifies the result as correct.

## Root Cause

The default branch dispatches on FILENAME and then acts on CONTENT it never looked at. `write_version_into` recognises four kinds by basename; everything else -- `VERSION`, `plain.txt`, `Cargo.lock`, a PDF -- takes the same branch and is overwritten wholesale. The branch is correct whenever its guess is right and destructive whenever it is wrong, and nothing distinguishes the two cases at the moment of writing.

Two callers reach it, which is what makes the guess look safe in review:

- `lib/cmd/version:107` -- each declared sidecar, in a loop.
- `lib/cmd/version:112` -- the version file itself, written LAST per invariant 1.

For the version file the guess is right by construction. For a sidecar it is an assumption about a file the project chose, and Conflab's choice breaks it.

`read_version` (`lib/helpers`) carries the matching assumption in its own `*)` branch -- `tr -d '[:space:]'` over the whole file -- which is why `check` reports permanent false drift rather than an unreadable file. The reader and the writer were deliberately kept in step; the comment at `lib/cmd/version:55` records why, having already been bitten once by them disagreeing. They agree here too. They agree on being wrong, which is why the two compose into a green verdict instead of an argument.

## Impact

WP-10 blocker. Conflab declares six sidecars, two of them `Cargo.lock`:

```
VERSION, native/cli/Cargo.toml, native/daemon/Cargo.toml,
native/cli/Cargo.lock, native/daemon/Cargo.lock,
native/macos/Conflab/Conflab/Info.plist
```

Conflab has a dedicated `sync_cargo_lock` helper for exactly this, and records why it must exist: `native/daemon/build.rs` enforces VERSION vs `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` parity and PANICS on drift, so a lockfile left behind fails the next `cargo build`. Devbin has no equivalent and does not fail -- it destroys.

Not raised to `critical` because both lockfiles are git-tracked and a `git checkout` recovers them. Not lowered below `high` because the gate certifies the destroyed tree as correct, so nothing downstream detects it and the destroyed file can be committed as clean. Of the four projects, Conflab is the only one declaring `Cargo.lock` sidecars; the general form applies to any project.

## Proposed Fix

Two parts, for the owner to rule on. Note what the first one must NOT do: `die` on every unrecognised sidecar would break `plain.txt`, which is documented and tested, so "refuse what we do not recognise" is the wrong shape.

1. **Make the default branch LOOK before it writes.** The bare write is correct exactly when the file already IS a bare version file, and that is checkable in one line: refuse when the existing content is not itself a lone version string. `plain.txt` (`1.2.3`) passes and keeps working; `Cargo.lock` (TOML) is refused by name. This stays on the right side of D1 and D7 -- it is a property of the file, not a recipe in config, and no project's config gains a regular expression. Refusing is safe by construction here because the version file is written last, so dying on a sidecar leaves a re-runnable tree, exactly as the PlistBuddy branch already argues at `lib/cmd/version:87`.

2. **Add a `Cargo.lock` recipe**, rewriting the `version` field of the named package entries only, so Conflab's declaration is served rather than merely refused. Conflab's `sync_cargo_lock` is the worked implementation and handles the daemon lock carrying only one of the two packages.

`read_version`'s `*)` branch needs the same guard, so `check` reports a file it cannot read rather than inventing a version out of the whole file.

Every fix needs a test verified RED against the current code. The obvious test -- assert the lockfile content is unchanged -- would pass against a `die` that never ran, so the test must assert the destination is byte-identical AND the command exited non-zero. The `plain.txt` path needs a test too, and it must go red against part 1 done carelessly: a guard written as "refuse anything not matching a known basename" passes every Cargo.lock test and silently breaks the documented case.

## Related

- ST0001 WP-10 -- the reference migration this blocks
- ST0001 WP-13 -- the pre-rollout review; this is the same class as R9, found by the same method after the review closed
- 0001 -- the prior issue, also found by running the real command rather than reading the design

## Resolutions

Fixed 2026-08-08 on the owner's authorisation, in three parts plus a documentation correction. Five tests, each verified RED against the code as it stood before the fix.

**1. The bare-version default now asks the FILE, not its name.** `is_bare_version` (`lib/helpers`, beside `assert_semver`) is the one predicate both the reader and the writer consult: a lone token that starts with a digit and carries only version characters. Deliberately looser than semver -- `0.6.0-rc1`, `1.4` and `20260808` all pass -- because its question is "is this a version string at all", not "is this project's numbering well-formed".

`write_version_into` takes a third argument, `role`. The version file passes `version-file` and keeps the unguarded write, because there the default is correct by construction -- it is the file `version_from` names. A sidecar takes the default role and is checked first. `read_version`'s own default branch asks the same predicate and returns `unknown` rather than the whole file.

Keying the guard on basenames instead would have been the easy version and it would have broken `plain.txt`, which is documented and tested. That case is what makes "ask the file" the right shape.

**2. `check` no longer calls an unreadable sidecar drifted.** "Drifted" is a claim about a comparison that happened; devbin had parsed nothing. `report_drift` now distinguishes the two and `check` reports each accordingly -- and it stops naming `version sync` as the cure for a file `sync` will refuse.

**3. There is deliberately NO `Cargo.lock` recipe**, and the reason is recorded at the site in `lib/cmd/version`. A lockfile carries a version per package, so a recipe must know which entries are the project's own. Bumping every entry matching the project version would corrupt any dependency sharing that number. Taking the names from the project's declared `Cargo.toml` sidecars does work for the writer -- but `read_version` lives in `lib/helpers`, which has no dependencies by rule (D15) and cannot consult config, so the reader could not follow. A recipe in the writer and absent from the reader is exactly the asymmetry `lib/cmd/version:55` was written to prevent. The guard refuses a `Cargo.lock` by name and says what to do instead; how a migrated project syncs its locks is that project's call.

**4. `docs/configuration.md` corrected.** It stated the old behaviour plainly -- "treats anything else as a bare version string" -- which is why this was a documented decision rather than an oversight, and why the sentence had to change with the code.

Verified end to end against the original reproduction: `check`, `sync` and `set` all refuse, the lockfile is byte-identical afterwards, and the version file is un-advanced so a re-run is clean. Both gates green.

Carried as AC-10.1 with AT-10.1 to AT-10.5.
